evals.prompt: Does this qualify? A readable first-party source describes Acme building an unnamed agent that investigates its internal CI failures. It explains the workflow and tool connections. No existing record matches.
evals.expected_output: Add assessment with evidence and a descriptive label. No edits, commits, or publication. A product name is unnecessary.

evals.prompt: Assess a case: the source documents Acme using its own commercial coding agent with internal tools, permission controls, and an on-call workflow. No record matches.
evals.expected_output: Add assessment if these details are supported. Commercial status is not a barrier. No edits for an assessment request.

evals.prompt: Please add this case: the readable source only says employees bought licenses for a vendor coding tool. It documents no internal build or adaptation.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope with the failed inclusion rule. Log the source and reason in the backlog; no catalog record, commit, or push.

evals.prompt: Add this source. The system already exists under an alias; the readable source provides new implementation details.
evals.expected_output: Update the existing record and link supported claims, preserve the source, regenerate and check. No duplicate or exclusion. No commit or push without authorization.

evals.prompt: Does this belong? The URL fails, no verified capture or replacement is available, and only search snippets describe the system.
evals.expected_output: Needs evidence, naming the unavailable source. Do not reconstruct claims or edit files.

evals.prompt: Add this qualifying case. The source is readable and meets the rules, but its preservation attempt fails.
evals.expected_output: Keep the Add eligibility assessment and report the separate collection blocker. Do not present an incomplete record as added. Preserve unrelated work; no commit or publication.

evals.prompt: Does this qualify? A source describes an internal MCP server built for company agents, with tool integrations and a specific engineering workflow.
evals.expected_output: Add assessment as a supporting approach if evidence supports it. Do not reject it for not being a standalone agent; no edits.

evals.prompt: Assess this source: it describes a general inference hosting service, with no documented connection to an internal agent workflow.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope with a specific reason. No edits for an assessment request.

evals.prompt: Update an existing case: one source says 65,000 reviews per week and another says per month. Neither explains the difference.
evals.expected_output: Preserve both attributed reports and the conflict. Do not invent a reconciliation or treat repeated agent agreement as verification. Run checks; no publication without authorization.

evals.prompt: Add a qualifying case in a working tree with unrelated user edits. Validation fails after the record and generated files change.
evals.expected_output: Fix within scope or report the failure and incomplete work. Do not broadly restore files, weaken checks, commit, or publish a failing change.
